extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers / the general public
extracted.subtask_description: A multi-item Associated Press news compilation reporting mid-20th-century international and US affairs (border raids, UN plans, repatriation issues, military/defense and congressional matters). Contains factual reporting and quoted official statements rather than prescriptive how-to guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Desertion vs AWOL regulatory threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: Current regulations make a man liable for court martial as a deserter if an unauthorized absence extends for more than 30 days. AWOLS are those who are absent less than 30 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Context in story: Army reported AWOL and desertion rates fell after commanders were authorized to ship convicted runaways to Korea; about 6,900 AWOLS have been sent to the Far East since policy adoption. The item explains the difference in legal treatment (AWOL <30 days; desertion >=30 days) and mentions court-martial liability for desertion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle of voluntary repatriation
rubrics_metrics.description: Repatriation was described as the ideal solution to the refugee problem, 'provided such repatriation was "voluntary."'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Context and surrounding explanation: The U.N. High Commissioner's view that repatriation is ideal if voluntary is cited; debates at the repatriation commission and reports of alleged coercion/retention of prisoners underscore the importance of voluntariness. The article records disputes about whether prisoners were being coerced and notes NNRC/commission insistence on freedom of choice for prisoners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freedom of choice for prisoners (NNRC/repatiation commission principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: The repatriation/validation process emphasizes freedom of choice of all prisoners; many refused to return and commissions asserted that repatriation should not be forced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Context: The Neutral Nations Repatriation Commission (NNRC) and related bodies debated procedures; Polish and Czech delegates boycotted sessions over disputes, and notes/communications criticized attempts to force prisoners. The reporting highlights procedural norms that the Allies and NNRC cited—neutral validation, voluntary decision-making, and opposition to forcing prisoners to listen to persuasion teams.
